title: InVEST Schistosomiasis
text: The goal of the Schistosomiasis plugin for the InVEST software is provide a tool to incorporate schistosomiasis risk into dam and water infrastructure development decisions. This work is based on the Walz et al. 2015 paper with additional contributions by Andy Chamberlain and Giulio De Leo from the De Leo Lab, and Lisa Mandle and Doug Denu from the Natural Capital Project.

title: Downloading InVEST and the Schistosomiasis Plugin
text:
The Schistosomiasis Tool is built on top of NatCap’s InVEST Workbench software. Before using the tool, you will have to download InVEST Workbench.



Windows users must confirm that the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable is installed. To check if you have the compiler installed you can:

Open Add or Remove Programs in Settings \> Apps \> Installed apps
Search for C++
You’ll see something like Microsoft Visual 2015-2019 Redistributable...
If you don’t see anything like that you’ll need to install the compiler

To install the compiler

Go to this link
Download and install Visual Studio 2026 using the Community option.
Alternatively you can just install Download and install the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable from this link. Both the x86 and x64 versions.
Open the .exe files and follow to installation prompts.

Download and install the InVEST workbench

Download InVEST and open the .exe file
Open your downloads folder and open the .exe file
A box Windows protexted your PC will open. Click More info and Run anyways

Follow the installation prompts







Download and install the InVEST workbench

Download InVEST
Open your downloads folder and open the .exe file
Once the file has downloaded, open it and click Agree when the license prompt appears.

A window will appear telling you to drag InVEST to Applications. Drag the InVEST app to your Applications folder.

IMPORTANT: Launch InVEST for the First Time. MacOS security will block the app on first launch. To allow it:

Open Applications

Right-click the InVEST app \(\to\) choose Open

In the popup, click Done (the app will not open yet)

Open Applications \(\to\) System Settings \(\to\) Privacy & Security

Scroll to the Security section and you should see: InVEST  Workbench was blocked to protect your Mac. Click Open Anyway.

Click Open Anyway again on the pop up box.

Enter your Mac username + password when prompted.


The InVEST Workbench will now start as usual. This approval is only needed the first time.

title: Downloading InVEST and the Schistosomiasis Plugin
text:
Installing the Schistosomiasis Plug-in
Once InVEST Workbench is downloaded, you will need to open it and add the Schistosomiasis Plug-in to use the Schistosomiasis Tool.

Open InVEST Workbench. In InVEST Workbench click the three line menu icon \(\to\) Manage Plugins \(\to\) Add Plugin.

Install plugin:

Copy and paste the following for git URL: https://github.com/natcap/invest-schistosomiasis.git.
Copy and paste the following for the Branch, tag or commit: feature/refactor-plugin-registry-compatible.
Check the box to acknowledge the risks associated with installing the plugin. Leave everything else blank.
Click Add. This step will take several minutes. It is setting up an isolated python environment, downloading, and installing the schistosomiasis model. You only need to do this step once. If you recieve and error message about long paths on Windows, open setting and search “long paths” then enable long paths.


The Schistosomiasis plugin is now available in the workbench.

The elements of the workbench are described in the InVEST documentation.

title: Downloading InVEST and the Schistosomiasis Plugin
text:
Updating the plugin
                                                                                                                                                                                 The plugin is still a work in progress. We will be updating it as feature are added. To update the plugin the current version must be uninstalled then the new version installed. 

Open InVEST and navigate to Manage plugins
Scroll to Remove a plugin
Select the Schistosmiasis plugin from the drop down menu
Click Remove

Using the new Branch, tag, or commit repeat the install process from above.

title: Pemba elimination scenario
text: Pemba Island, Tanzania is nearing elimination of schistosomiasis. Here we use risk maps derived from 2012, 2019, and 2025 to compare risk to human-case data.
